definitions.explanation: A bag filled with ice or cold water, applied to the body to reduce swelling, cool fever, or treat injuries.

examples.japanese: {氷嚢|ひょうのう}を{頭|あたま}に{当|あ}てた。
examples.english: I put an ice bag on my head.

examples.japanese: {熱|ねつ}が{出|で}たので{氷嚢|ひょうのう}で{額|ひたい}を{冷|ひ}やした。
examples.english: I had a fever, so I cooled my forehead with an ice bag.

examples.japanese: {足首|あしくび}を{捻挫|ねんざ}したときは、まず{氷嚢|ひょうのう}で{患部|かんぶ}を{冷|ひ}やして{腫|は}れを{抑|おさ}えることが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: When you sprain your ankle, it's important to first cool the affected area with an ice pack to reduce swelling.

notes:
A compound of {氷|ひょう} (ice) and {嚢|のう} (bag, sac). Refers to the classic rubber or fabric bag filled with ice cubes and water, used for cooling the body.

The traditional {氷嚢|ひょうのう} — a round rubber bag with a screw cap — is an iconic item in Japanese homes, often associated with sick days and fever care. Modern versions include reusable gel packs and sports-specific ice bags.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {氷嚢|ひょうのう}を{当|あ}てる: to apply an ice bag
- {氷嚢|ひょうのう}で{冷|ひ}やす: to cool with an ice bag
- {氷嚢|ひょうのう}を{作|つく}る: to prepare an ice bag

SIMILAR WORDS:
- アイスパック: ice pack — loanword, often refers to gel-type cold packs
- {冷却|れいきゃく}シート: cooling sheet — adhesive gel sheets applied to the forehead
- {湯|ゆ}たんぽ: hot water bottle — the warm counterpart, used for heating
